data.text: Just some context on how insane this is: A ruptured patellar tendon is one of the toughest injuries for an NFL player to come back from. It usually requires close to a year of recovery. It’s especially difficult for an OL because of the constant force and explosive knee extension required on every snap. Trapilo ruptured his in January and is already off PUP in August. That’s not normal.

data.text: #Titans preseason game one initial thoughts (starting with the bad): 1. Cam Ward played poorly. Questionable decisions, poor accuracy. Bad game. One of his worst as a Titan. That said, it’s three drives of a preseason game… 2. First team defense was uninspiring against Niners QB3 and backups. Little pass rush. Didn’t look particularly disruptive. 3. Secondary gets its own line item because it was abysmal. 49ers WRs wide open frequently. When they weren’t, Titans corners routinely got beat at the catch point. Letting Kurtis Rourke go 12 of 14 is shameful. 4. First team OL was a legitimate bright spot, especially in the run game. Rookie RG Fernando Carmona looked like he belonged in the starting lineup. Got folded up on one run but was otherwise very good. Latham looked outstanding. 5. Related… Titans RBs all looked good. Pollard with the TD. Spears elusive. Singleton runs hard and has real juice (needs some work in pass pro though). 6. Joey Slye with a monster 4-4 night including makes from 53, 55, and 58. Good response from him to a rough scrimmage last week.

data.text: Some late practice notes (these late practices are killing my workflow!): • Wanted to provide more detail on the final period of practice because I've never seen anything like it. They set up a 10-minute overtime period with the 1's against the 1's and the 2's against the 2's. The second-team offense got the ball first, presumably setting up the first-team offense with the chance to drive for the "win." It didn't exactly work out that way. Both offenses sputtered. The 2's went three-and-out on their first drive and Harbaugh then had long snapper Ben Mann, punter Jordan Stout and a punt returner (Calvin Austin) as the only players on the field. Stout boomed a punt 60 yards for a touchback. On the 1's first drive, Jaxson Dart hit Isaiah Likely for a 13-yard gain on a curl for their lone first down. Malachi Fields dropped a well-thrown back-shoulder fade to stall the drive. Stout then had a 41-yard punt to Xavier Gipson. The 2's got one first down on a 10-yard in route by Thomas Fidone. Stout then kicked a 56-yard touchback with Braxton Berrios back to return. A hold on the first play (a Cam Skattebo run off right tackle) killed the next drive. It looked like Abdul Carter and Darius Alexander combined for a sack on third-and-long. Stout then boomed a 61-yard punt to the other 20-yard line. The second-team offense operated the hurry-up after taking over at their own 20 with two minutes remaining. Isaiah Hodgins and Dalen Cambre had first-down catches before the offense faced fourth-and-3 from the opposing 47. Jameis Winston hit Cambre on a quick out for 3 yards to keep the drive alive. Three straight incompletions, including an Odell catch along the sideline that was ruled out of bounds and a PBU by Art Green, set up fourth-and-10 from the 44. It wasn't clear what the coaches were going to do, but Cam Skattebo and Isaiah Likely pleaded with the coaches to let Dominic Zvada to attempt a 62-yard field goal. With the wind at his back, Zvada drilled the kick with room to spare. • Tremaine Edmunds jumped a curl on the first play of practice and nearly had an interception. Two plays later he tipped pass while chasing Dart out of the pocket. Edmunds has really good ball skills for a LB. There have been a lot of tipped balls in camp from all the QBs, which signals it's an emphasis of the defense. • Korie Black mixed in with Deonte Banks and Colton Hood as a first-team corner. Huge opportunity upcoming for Black with so many corners injured. • After spending the first two weeks of camp almost exclusively on the third-team OL, Evan Neal has gotten some second-team reps at LG this week. It's now or never for the former first-round pick.
